## Installation

You can install the development version of dawgma from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rforbiodatascience26/group_18_package")
```


```{r setup}
library(dawgma)
```

---
link to gitHub: https://github.com/rforbiodatascience26/group_18_package/tree/master 

DNA_create() makes a random DNA string and takes the DNA string length as an argument.
```{r}
DNA_str <- DNA_create(27)
DNA_str
```

DNA_to_RNA() takes a string of DNA and transforms it to RNA
```{r}
RNA_str <- DNA_to_RNA(DNA_str)
RNA_str
```

codon() takes an string and splits it up in codons.
```{r}
codon_vector <- codon(RNA_str)
codon_vector
```

translate_codons() takes a vector of codon strings and translates it to amino acids. It returns a string of amino acids.

```{r}
aminoacids <- translate_codons(codon_vector)
aminoacids
```

plot_aa() takes a string of aminoacids and plots their frequency in the string.
```{r}
plot_aa(aminoacids)
```
